newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkey and northern Cyprus edge toward integration.
newsitem.headline: Turkey and northern Cyprus edge toward integration.

text.p: Turkey and northern Cyprus on Wednesday agreed to work towards partial integration, just five days before the start of U.N.-sponsored talks to resolve the dispute between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.

The agreement, signed by the foreign ministers of Turkey and northern Cyprus, calls for an Association Council to work towards the partial economic and defence integration of Turkey with the breakaway northern part of the Mediterranean island.
Turkey has warned it will unite with the north if Greek Cyprus begins membership talks with the European Union. The EU has invited Greek Cyprus to begin talks on joining the Union next year.
Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash and Greek Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides are expected to meet in Montreux, Switzerland, on August 11.
The two met in New York state under the auspices of the United Nations last month in an attempt to revive stalled negotiations on reunifying Cyprus as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.

They have held follow-up talks in Nicosia at which they reached an agreement that could lead to the opening of unmarked graves of people missing in hostilities between Cyprus's Greek and Turkish communities.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded in response to a coup backed by the military then ruling Greece.
A Turkish Cypriot state in the north, headed by Denktash, was declared in 1983 but is recognised only by Ankara.
